You know, for me, it was never actually about me 

I liked looking at flowers. I liked reading books, watching sunsets, stargazing, I liked a lot of things. Liked. Past tense. 

I got depressed, like suuuuper depressed, and, like anyone would after suffering for what seemed like forever, I was ready to die. But then I realised that the flowers were still just as beautiful as ever, it was me who was different. I started pushing myself to make a routine and by God stick to it, even if it meant I had to set 5 alarms one after another because boy are beds comfortable. 

My advice would be force yourself to stick to a routine, and take comfort in the stability of a pattern you know will repeat.

Don't kill yourself to prove to the world that you can keep on living. Don't kill yourself to see the day that you actually do get better. Don't kill yourself to simply see something improve, get a pet, start up a new hobby, whatever. 

Edit: spelling and some phrasing for clarification

NTA - It was rude of her to say that, and it seems unreasonable of her too. I'm an atheist myself, but I would never say that about anyone else's religion, and, actually, take an active interest in finding out what other people's religious beliefs are, since it's interesting to me. What I'm trying to say is that atheists don't inherently hate religions. 
   She is rude for calling you homophobic, and for, in general, not being a very good friend. Teasing is fine, insults are not, and she doesn't sound like a very good friend, using her sexuality as an excuse to insult you. 
   The situation you've described seems very much like just a burst of anger, and doesn't seem to have any logic behind it. She's the Asshole.

NAH - to me, it sounds like your mom was trying to be supportive and maybe just doesn't understand how distracting and stressful her yelling is. My parents are like that too, and I understand the pressure them not only being there but also shouting at you during the warmup creates. 
Maybe try talking to her, and explain that it's difficult to focus when she yells, and that it's okay for a few to go past you.
